answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a bond before it may earn fees or vote, while randomly pairing it with unrelated agents for challenge-response tasks and auditing its transaction graph. A fake cluster must lock fresh capital for every persona, cannot cheaply manufacture trusted history, and risks having the whole bond slashed when collusion is detected. Thus a sparrow-sized attacker faces a canyon of upfront collateral, and every new thread of identities increases exposure rather than leverage.
